post.caption:
Dad saved 11 years for Hajj. You’ve skipped salah for 11 days. 🤍

6:05 p.m., a bus stop in the rain. Your mum sends a photo she found in the cupboard: Mina, 2014. Dad in two white sheets, smiling. On the back, in his handwriting: “Here I asked Allah for one thing: that my son prays.”

“Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant.” (2:222)

Tonight at Isha: come back. One prayer is enough to start.

captions: 6:05 p.m. The bus stop. Rain on the glass.
Your mum sends a photo. “Look what I found in the cupboard.”
Mina, 2014. Dad in two white sheets, smiling.
Three million people. No titles. No brands. Just white.
He saved one coin at a time. 11 years, for this road.
On the back of the photo, in his handwriting:
“Here I asked Allah for one thing: that my son prays.”
11 years for that road. And you, 11 days away.
7:10 p.m. Isha. The masjid by the bus stop.
Row three. Shoes off. Your hands still cold from the rain.
“Allahu akbar.” Eleven days end in two words.
After, you call Dad. He hears it in your voice.
